done.why: I got told I'd used all 30 turns right as I was heading back west from a dead-end beach. I was actually still interested enough to keep going for a bit, so the cap, not boredom, stopped me.

about: A white house in a field with a trapdoor down into caves. You grab a lamp and a sword, fight a troll with an axe, and then poke around underground rooms looking for treasure like the platinum bar. The underground seems to have been damaged somehow: cave-ins block passages in the round room, and there's a beach by white cliffs that leads nowhere.

moments.note: The trapdoor slammed shut behind me and someone barred it. Who? That got my attention.
The sword glowing brighter as I got near the troll was a nice tell, and the fight started immediately.
The troll fight dragged on for six swings. I was typing the same line over and over and the outcomes felt random.
Black fog swallowing the troll's body was a weird little touch I liked.
Round Room says passages are blocked by cave-ins but doesn't say which ones. I just guessed east.
Typing 'take bar' and getting 'Bar bar ...' back was funny and made me want to figure the room out.
Saying 'echo' actually changed the room and let me take the platinum bar. Felt clever.
Walked south along the beach and it was just a dead end with nothing on it.
Turn cap hit mid-move, right when I'd found a loop of rooms I wanted to finish exploring.

wished: I wished the Round Room told me which passages were caved in instead of making me guess directions.
I wished the troll fight were shorter or that I had some choice other than typing the same attack line six times.
I wished the beach had something on it, or at least a reason to walk down there.
I wished I could have asked who barred the trapdoor, or found some sign of them.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: First hint that there's somebody else in this house. Made me want to know who.

lines.line: Almost as soon as the troll breathes his last breath, a cloud of sinister black fog envelops him, and when the fog lifts, the carcass has disappeared.
lines.why: Odd and creepy, and a reward for the slog of the fight.

lines.line: Several of them have unfortunately been blocked by cave-ins.
lines.why: This is where it felt like something had happened to the place. It's also where I didn't know where to go.
The joke landed and made the room a puzzle I wanted to solve instead of just a loud room.

lines.line: The acoustics of the room change subtly.
lines.why: Told me my guess worked without spelling it out.

fun.why: The house, the trapdoor slam, and the echo trick were fun. The six-turn troll fight and the empty beach were not.

engagement.why: I was still going when the cap hit, which says something, but the fight and the dead end both had me close to quitting.

difficulty.why: Nothing hard so far. The troll is a matter of repeating one command; the echo room took one guess. The only real obstacle was not knowing which way wasn't caved in.

interestingness.why: The cave-ins and the person barring the door hint at a story that I didn't get far enough to see. The beach was flat.

prose.why: Short, clear room descriptions, and the fight and troll-death lines have personality. The beach rooms were thin.
